# 🦉 The Daily Prophet

A weather risk intelligence agent for a logistics company's US distribution hubs.
Analysts chat with it to find out which hubs are most exposed to severe weather, compare hubs,
and understand *why* a hub is risky, to help decide where to invest in resilience upgrades.

> 🚧 Work in progress. Built step by step. See [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md).

## Docs
- [Plan](docs/plan.md): architecture, tables, steps
- [Decision log](docs/decisions.md): every choice and why
- [Assumptions, uncertainty & scope](docs/assumptions.md)
- [Design](docs/design.md)
- [AI session log](docs/session/): the full conversation with the coding agent

## Run locally
Requirements: Node 22+, a Supabase project.

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local     # then fill in the values (see comments in the file)
npm run db:check               # verifies the database connection: lists the hubs
npm run dev                    # http://localhost:3000
```

## Scripts
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Start the app locally |
| `npm test` | Unit tests (Vitest) |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint (includes the rule keeping `src/core` free of Next.js) |
| `npm run db:check` | Connect to Supabase and list hubs per region |
| `npm run ingest` | Fetch FEMA + Open-Meteo data for all active hubs (incremental; the first full load takes about 1 h because of Open-Meteo's rate limits) |
| `npm run ingest -- --hub=dallas,denver` | Same, for selected hubs only |
| `npm run ingest -- --refresh-fema` | Re-fetch FEMA records for every hub (e.g. after a new NRI release) |
| `npm run score` | Re-score all hubs from stored data (no API calls). The ingest runs this automatically. |
| `npm run ask -- "question"` | Ask the real agent from the terminal (add `--session=<id>` for a follow-up, `--metric` for metric units) |

## Summary

Step 5 of [the plan](docs/plan.md): **the API.** The chat endpoint streams progress and the answer live, a widgets endpoint feeds the dashboard, a nightly cron refreshes the data, everything sits behind a login, and every error is friendly (UX-first).

```text
browser ──Basic Auth──▶ src/proxy.ts (layer 1)        /api/cron/* excluded
                          │
POST /api/chat ──requireSiteAuth (layer 2)──▶ chatRequestSchema.parse
   └─ createUIMessageStreamResponse(buildChatStream(body, answerQuestion))   # src/core/api/chatStream.ts
        start → data-session → data-progress ×N (in place) → text deltas
        → [data-retry → text again] → data-answer (validated) | data-error {code,message,hint,retryable} → finish

GET /api/widgets ──connection() → requireSiteAuth → loadWidgetsData → buildWidgetsData (pure)
GET /api/cron/ingest ──connection() → Bearer CRON_SECRET → runIngestThenScore("cron")   # vercel.json 06:00 UTC
```

```text
src/proxy.ts                      Basic Auth (pages + APIs), friendly 401
src/app/api/_lib/http.ts          json · errorResponse · failure (logs 🦄) · requireSiteAuth · requireCronAuth
src/app/api/chat|widgets|cron/…   thin routes
src/core/api/chatStream.ts        stream builder (framework-free, tested)
src/core/api/progressLabels.ts    "Breaking down Dallas's risk score…" (all progress copy)
src/core/errors/userErrors.ts     ALL user-facing error copy
src/core/security/auth.ts         Basic Auth parse + constant-time compare + cron bearer
src/core/widgets/                 buildWidgetsData (pure) · loadWidgetsData
vercel.json                       cron 0 6 * * *
```

## Decisions (D73–D79, round A1–A5)

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D73 | Chat stream events: session → progress (in place) → text → retry → answer \| error | Live progress, but the UI only trusts the **validated** answer |
| D74 | **Two auth layers**: proxy + per-route re-check, constant-time compare | Next 16 docs: proxy alone isn't full authorization |
| D75 | Cron 06:00 UTC, same pipeline as the CLI, 300 s limit (measured 60 s) | Yesterday's data is ready by then |
| D76 | **Friendly errors** `{ code, message, hint, retryable }`, all copy in one file, streamed as structured `data-error` | "Even friendlier, UX is top-notch". Honest model-failure copy |
| D77 | `/api/widgets`: top 5, hazard leaders, freshness (pure function) | Deterministic dashboard data |
| D78 | `await connection()` first in GET routes | Build-time prerender "bail out" was being swallowed by try/catch |
| D79 | `AgentInputError` moved to `core/errors`, with friendlier messages | Cleaner dependencies |

**Friendly error copy** (from `userErrors.ts`):

| Code | Status | Message → hint |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_request` | 400 | "I couldn't quite read that question." → "Try asking it in a sentence or two…" |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | "Please sign in to use The Daily Prophet." → "Use the username and password you were given…" |
| `no_data` | 503 | "Today's weather data hasn't landed yet. 🐱" → "Scores refresh every night…" (retryable) |
| `agent_failed` | 502 | "I couldn't put together an answer I can stand behind this time." → "I'd rather say so than guess…" (retryable) |
| `internal_error` | 500 | "Something went wrong on our side. 😿" → "It's not you — please try again in a moment…" (retryable) |

- the stream event order
- the retry text reset
- friendly `data-error` with no internals
- Basic Auth parsing and constant-time compare
- cron bearer
- error classification, with "never leaks internals" checked
- progress labels
- widget data

**Live smoke test** (`next start`, curl):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| widgets, no login | `401` + `WWW-Authenticate` + friendly JSON |
| widgets, wrong password | `401` friendly JSON |
| widgets, signed in | top: New Orleans 73.9, Tampa 72.9, Dallas 72.4, Jacksonville 70, OKC 69.6. Leaders: hurricane Jacksonville, winter SLC 94.3, flood Houston 84, storms Dallas, wind OKC 85.5, heat Phoenix. Weather through 2026-11-24 |
| page, no login | `401` + browser login prompt + friendly text |
| chat, bad body | `400` "I couldn't quite read that question." + hint |
| cron, no secret | `401` |
| **chat, streamed** (Midwest winter) | `data-session` → 4 progress lines ("Ranking hubs by winter exposure in the Midwest…", "Comparing Minneapolis, Detroit and St. Louis…") → 86 text deltas → `data-answer`, **validated text identical to streamed text** |
| **cron, with secret** | `{"ok":true,"hubs":36,"weatherRowsSaved":252,"hubsScored":36,"failedHubs":[]}` in **60 s** |

## ⚠️ Security note (my mistake, flagged honestly)

While smoke-testing I loaded `.env.local` with bash `source`. A value with special characters made bash print **a 4-character fragment of `CRON_SECRET`** into the session log.
- **Fix:** I'm asking Yarden to rotate `CRON_SECRET`.
- **Session log:** held out of this PR until the rotation, so a stale fragment is all that remains.
- **Prevention:** lesson #13 in `CLAUDE.md` (never `source` env files; read them with Node).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** medium

`proxy.ts` now gates **every** page and API route:
- a deploy without `APP_USERNAME` / `APP_PASSWORD` / `CRON_SECRET` set shows "isn't configured yet" (500)
- the Step 10 deploy must set all three in Vercel
- the nightly job only runs once deployed

## Env vars

`APP_USERNAME`, `APP_PASSWORD` (≥ 12 characters) and `CRON_SECRET` (≥ 16 characters) are validated by Zod and covered by the `.env.example` drift test.

The chat UI on top of this stream, the widgets, per-answer charts, and the US/Metric switch.

content.text:
**[PR #6](https://github.com/yardenfarag/Home-Assignment-Moveo/pull/6) is open: the API is done and tested live.** 158 tests pass, along with the type check, lint and build.

**What it adds:**
- **Live chat.** Each question first shows short progress lines ("Ranking hubs by winter exposure in the Midwest…"), then the answer appears as it's written. In the live test the final answer matched the streamed text exactly, and the same check-and-retry rules apply as in Step 4.
- **Widgets data.** Top 5 hubs, the leading hub for each hazard, and how fresh the data is.
- **Nightly update.** Fetches new weather and re-scores every hub at 06:00 UTC. Live run: 60 s, 36 hubs, no failures.
- **Login.** Every page and API route asks for your username and password, checked at the edge and again inside each route. The nightly job uses its own secret instead.
- **Friendly errors.** Every error has a warm message, a hint about what to do, and a "Try again" signal. All the wording is in one file. The model-failure message stays honest: *"I couldn't put together an answer I can stand behind this time… I'd rather say so than guess."*
- **A Next.js 16 build issue, now fixed.** During the build, Next tried to pre-render the GET routes, and my error handling was hiding the signal it uses to stop. Calling `connection()` first is the documented fix.

**⚠️ One thing that needs you.** While testing, I loaded `.env.local` in a way that made the shell print **4 characters of your `CRON_SECRET`** into the session log. That was my mistake. The risk is low (4 of 24 characters), but the repo and log are public, so please **rotate it**:
- **Option A:** I generate a new one and write it straight into `.env.local` without displaying it (URL-safe characters only, so this can't happen again).
- **Option B:** You replace it yourself.

The session-log update is **held out of PR #6** until then. After rotation the fragment is useless, and I'll include the log in the next PR. I've also added lesson #13 to `CLAUDE.md` so this doesn't happen again: never load `.env` files through the shell.

**Next is Step 6, the UI:**
- the chat screen on top of this stream
- the dashboard widgets

It matches: `@ai-sdk/react` 4.0.186 pins `ai` 7.0.181, exactly our version, and supports React 19.3.

## Step 6: the UI, design round

Here's the layout I'm proposing (desktop):

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 🦉 The Daily Prophet            Weather risk for 36 hubs · data thru Nov 24   │
│                                              [ US | Metric ]  [+ New chat]     │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┤
│                                              │ ╭ Top risk hubs ─────────────╮ │
│  (empty state)                               │ │ 1 New Orleans ███████ 73.9 H│ │
│   🐱 Ask about weather risk at our hubs.     │ │ 2 Tampa       ███████ 72.9 H│ │
│   [Which Midwest hubs are most exposed…]     │ │ 3 Dallas      ███████ 72.4 H│ │
│   [Compare Miami and Houston…]               │ ╰─────────────────────────────╯ │
│   [% of Denver days with snow last year?]    │ ╭ Hazard leaders ────────────╮ │
│   [Why is Dallas's risk high?]               │ │ 🌀 Jacksonville 100         │ │
│                                              │ │ ❄  Salt Lake City 94.3      │ │
│  ╭ answer card (glass) ─────────────────╮    │ │ 🌊 Houston 84   …           │ │
│  │ ⚠ Heads-up: Seattle isn't High — Low │    │ ╰─────────────────────────────╯ │
│  │ answer text (Markdown)               │    │ ╭ Data status ───────────────╮ │
│  │ ▇▇▇▇ chart from tool results          │    │ │ Weather thru Nov 24 · FEMA │ │
│  │ ● High confidence  ▸ Assumptions…    │    │ │ NRI Dec 2025 · scored 06:00│ │
│  │ ▸ How I got this   [follow-up chips] │    │ ╰─────────────────────────────╯ │
│  ╰──────────────────────────────────────╯    │                                │
│  [ Ask about a hub, hazard or region…   ➤ ] │                                │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

❓ **U1** - **Layout.** Chat on the left (about 62%), widgets column on the right. On mobile the widgets become a swipeable strip above the chat. The header holds the name, data freshness, the **US/Metric switch**, and **New chat**.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **U2** - **The answer card, top to bottom:**
1. A **premise banner** when the question's assumption is wrong, e.g. "Heads-up: Seattle's hurricane risk isn't High — it's Low."
2. The answer text.
3. A **chart** built from the tool results (U3).
4. A **confidence badge**, with its reason on hover or tap.
5. A **recommendation box** with the disclaimer, for decision questions.
6. Collapsible **"Assumptions & limits"**.
7. Collapsible **"How I got this"**, listing the tools used.
8. **Follow-up chips** you can click.

While it's working, the card shows the live progress lines, then the text with a cursor. On a retry: "Double-checking my numbers…". On failure: a soft card with the hint and a **Try again** button.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **U3** - **Charts**, chosen by code from the tools used, never by the LLM. All use the Recharts library from the plan:
- **rank** → horizontal bars
- **compare** → grouped bars per hazard
- **weather stat** → big number + "33 of 365 days"
- **explain** → per-hazard bars that show the observed vs FEMA halves, plus the formula line

**Colors:** colorblind-safe Low (blue) / Medium (amber) / High (coral), and **every color always comes with a text label**, never color alone.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **U4** - **The units switch needs a small API change.** The weather-stat tool currently writes its threshold in whichever unit system was active when the question was asked. To make the switch flip panels instantly (D60), it will return the threshold in **both** systems.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **U5** - **After a page refresh: start fresh, or restore the conversation?**
- **(a) Start fresh.** New chat on refresh. No extra code.
- **(b) Restore.** The server already stores the history (D25), so it needs a small `GET /api/chat/history?sessionId=…` endpoint and a loading state.

➡️ **(b).** It's cheap since the data is already stored, and losing a conversation on refresh is bad UX. "New chat" still starts fresh on purpose.

---

❓ **U6** - **Three new dependencies:**
- `@ai-sdk/react` for `useChat` (verified compatible with our `ai` 7.0.181)
- `recharts` (in the plan)
- `react-markdown` to render answers safely (no raw HTML)

The alternative is hand-writing the stream reader and a Markdown renderer: more code, more bugs.

➡️ Yes to all three.

---

❓ **U7** - **Accessibility and polish:**
- the streaming answer is announced to screen readers
- full keyboard use, with Enter to send and Shift+Enter for a new line
- visible focus rings
- reduced-motion respected
- AA contrast on the glass surfaces
- data attribution (Open-Meteo CC BY 4.0, FEMA) in a small footer

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **U8** - **A little personality, kept light:** a 🐱 in the empty state and in friendly errors (already in the copy), and the owl as the wordmark. Data and answers stay plain and professional, with no emojis inside answers.

➡️ Yes.

On U8 I'm taking your final word: **keep the cats.** The light 🐱 touches stay in the empty state and friendly errors, with the owl as the wordmark, and answers stay professional.

**On U3, honestly: you're right.** Most of my proposed charts would just **repeat the numbers the answer already states**. "Minneapolis 86.5, Detroit 70.3…" followed by a bar chart of 86.5 and 70.3 adds clutter, not insight. A visual earns its place only if it shows something the text *can't* show at a glance. Three do:

| Question type | Instead of a bar chart | What it shows that text can't |
|---|---|---|
| **"Why is X high?"** | **Score breakdown**: one strip showing how much each hazard contributes (weight × score), plus the "worst hazard" boost, adding up to the overall | *Where the score comes from*, in one look, e.g. Dallas = storms + heat + flood |
| **"Compare A and B"** | **Comparison grid**: hubs × 6 hazards, each cell a score with a level color and text | The whole picture at once. Text can only walk through it line by line |
| **"How often did it snow?"** | **Seasonality strip**: hazard days by month across the period | **When** it happens (Denver's snow is Oct–Apr), a planning fact the answer doesn't give |
| Rankings | **No chart**: a clean ranked list with level chips | The list *is* the visual |

These are simple enough to build in plain HTML/CSS, with no chart library at all. That's one dependency fewer and lighter pages. The seasonality strip needs the weather-stat tool to also return **counts by month**. That's still code-computed, so the honesty rules are unaffected.

---

❓ **U3b** - Replace the charts with these three purposeful visuals (score breakdown, comparison grid, seasonality strip), a ranked list for rankings, and **drop Recharts**.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **U5b** - **Chat history side nav, and who sees which chats.** Refresh starts a new chat, "New chat" does too, and a side nav lists earlier chats. One catch: everyone shares **one login**, so the server can't tell users apart. A list of "all chats" would show every visitor's conversations to everyone.
- **(a) This browser's chats only.** The browser remembers its own session IDs, and the side nav shows their titles and dates, fetched from the server.
- **(b) All chats on the site.** Shared with everyone who has the login.

Either way it needs two small endpoints: `GET /api/chat/sessions?ids=…` (titles and dates) and `GET /api/chat/history?sessionId=…` (reopen a chat). Past answers come back exactly as they were validated, data panels included.

➡️ **(a).** It's private by default and matches what "my old chats" means. Real per-user history would need real accounts, which can come later with the themed login page.

u3b- accepted.
u5b-a

Both settled: **three purposeful visuals and no chart library**, and the **chat history side nav lists only this browser's chats**.

| D79 | `AgentInputError` moved to `core/errors/`, and its messages are friendlier ("That message is too long for me — please keep it under 1,000 characters."). | Error classes belong with errors. The error module no longer pulls in the whole agent. |

### UI details (Step 6, round U1–U8)
| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D80 | **Layout** (U1): side nav (chats) · chat · overview column. Phone: the overview becomes a **swipe strip** above the chat. Tablet: a row of three. Desktop: the right column. Dark glass, Roboto. | The chat stays primary on every screen size. |
| D81 | **The answer card** (U2), top to bottom: premise banner (code-decided) → text → visuals → recommendation (with disclaimer) → confidence → collapsible "Assumptions & limits" and "How I got this" → follow-up chips. While it works: live progress lines, then streaming text. On a failed check: "Double-checking my numbers…". On failure: a soft card with a hint and "Try again". | Live but trustworthy: only the validated answer gets the data panel. |
| D82 | **Visuals only where they add something the text can't** (U3, U3b, Yarden: "are visuals adding value?"). **Score breakdown** (where a hub's score comes from), **comparison grid** (hubs × hazards at a glance), **seasonality strip** (*when* hazard days happen), and a plain **ranked list** for rankings. Built in HTML/CSS, **no chart library** (Recharts dropped). Chosen by code from the tool results, at most 2 per answer. | Bar charts of numbers the text already states are clutter. Each kept visual answers a question the prose can't. |
| D83 | **US/Metric switch** (U4): the weather-stat tool also returns its threshold in both systems (`thresholdBySystem`) and counts by month (`byMonth`). The explain tool returns each hazard's points (`contributions`, `worstHazardBoost`). All computed in code. | The switch flips panels instantly (D60), and the visuals never do arithmetic in the browser. |
| D84 | **Chat history** (U5, U5b): a refresh starts a new chat, the side nav lists **this browser's chats only** (ids in localStorage), and opening one restores its questions and validated answers. New endpoints: `GET /api/chat/sessions?ids=…`, `GET /api/chat/history?sessionId=…`. Retry feedback is hidden from transcripts. | Everyone shares one login, so "all chats" would expose other visitors' conversations. Real per-user history needs real accounts (later). |
| D85 | **Dependencies** (U6): `@ai-sdk/react` 4.0.186 (pins our `ai` 7.0.181) for `useChat`, and `react-markdown` (no raw HTML). | Standard, less custom code. Verified compatible before installing. |
| D86 | **Accessibility** (U7): the streaming answer is announced (`aria-live`), Enter sends / Shift+Enter adds a line, native `<details>`, visible focus rings, reduced motion respected, colors always paired with text labels. **Personality** (U8): the cat in the empty state and friendly errors, the owl wordmark. Answers stay plain. | Readability first, a little warmth around it. |
| D87 | **Tool output types are imported by the UI** from exported tool builder functions (`ExplainHubScoreOutput`, …). No duplicated shapes. | Single source of truth: a tool change can't silently break a visual. |
| D88 | **No Markdown tables in answers** (prompt rule). The UI draws grids from the data. | A model-written table rendered as raw pipes, and it duplicated the comparison grid. |

# 🦉 The Daily Prophet

A weather risk intelligence agent for a logistics company's US distribution hubs.
Analysts chat with it to find out which hubs are most exposed to severe weather, compare hubs,
and understand *why* a hub is risky, to help decide where to invest in resilience upgrades.

> 🚧 Work in progress. Built step by step. See [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md).

## Docs
- [Plan](docs/plan.md): architecture, tables, steps
- [Decision log](docs/decisions.md): every choice and why
- [Assumptions, uncertainty & scope](docs/assumptions.md)
- [Design](docs/design.md)
- [AI session log](docs/session/): the full conversation with the coding agent

## Run locally
Requirements: Node 22+, a Supabase project.

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local     # then fill in the values (see comments in the file)
npm run db:check               # verifies the database connection: lists the hubs
npm run dev                    # http://localhost:3000
```

## Scripts
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Start the app locally |
| `npm test` | Unit tests (Vitest) |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint (includes the rule keeping `src/core` free of Next.js) |
| `npm run db:check` | Connect to Supabase and list hubs per region |
| `npm run ingest` | Fetch FEMA + Open-Meteo data for all active hubs (incremental; the first full load takes about 1 h because of Open-Meteo's rate limits) |
| `npm run ingest -- --hub=dallas,denver` | Same, for selected hubs only |
| `npm run ingest -- --refresh-fema` | Re-fetch FEMA records for every hub (e.g. after a new NRI release) |
| `npm run score` | Re-score all hubs from stored data (no API calls). The ingest runs this automatically. |
| `npm run ask -- "question"` | Ask the real agent from the terminal (add `--session=<id>` for a follow-up, `--metric` for metric units) |
| `npm run fema:anchors` | Recompute the national 95th-percentile FEMA anchors (for review before changing `scoring/config.ts`) |
| `npm run session:export -- <file.jsonl>` | Export the AI session log to `docs/session/` (scrubbed) |

## API
Every route requires the site login (HTTP Basic Auth: `APP_USERNAME` / `APP_PASSWORD`), except the cron route.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/chat` | Body `{ "sessionId": null \| "<uuid>", "message": "…", "units": "us" \| "metric" }`. Streams the AI SDK chat protocol: `data-session`, `data-progress`, answer text, then `data-answer` (validated) or `data-error`. |
| `GET /api/widgets` | Top 5 hubs, the leading hub per hazard, data freshness. |
| `GET /api/cron/ingest` | Nightly job (Vercel Cron, 06:00 UTC): fetch new weather, then re-score. Needs `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>`. |

Errors are always friendly JSON: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "hint", "retryable" } }`.

```bash
curl -u "$APP_USERNAME:$APP_PASSWORD" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sessionId":null,"message":"Which Midwest hubs are most exposed to winter?","units":"us"}' \
  http://localhost:3000/api/chat
```

## Database
SQL migrations live in [supabase/migrations/](supabase/migrations/). Apply them in order to a fresh
Supabase project (SQL editor or Supabase CLI). The second migration seeds the 36 hubs.

## Data attribution
Weather data by [Open-Meteo.com](https://open-meteo.com/) (CC BY 4.0). Hazard data: FEMA National Risk Index.

lines: session log. Rotate any secret that leaks, even partially.
14. **A GET route handler logs "needs to bail out of prerendering"** → call `await connection()` first, outside any
try/catch (Cache Components tries to prerender GET handlers, and catching its signal hides it).
+15. **A phone layout is wider than the screen** → a grid track grew to fit a non-wrapping child (e.g. a swipe strip).
+   Use `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)]` and `min-w-0` on the grid item.
+16. **A Tailwind class doesn't override a custom class** → custom CSS outside `@layer` beats Tailwind's layered
+   utilities. Put shared classes like `.glass` in `@layer components`.
+17. **Stopping a background `npx next start` leaves the port busy** → the `npx` wrapper dies but its Node child
+   keeps serving the OLD build. Start servers with `node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next start`, and check the port
+18. **Judging UI from code** → drive the real app and look at screenshots (headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol
+   with an Authorization header). Three layout bugs were invisible in the code and obvious in the screenshots.

## Summary

Step 6 of [the plan](docs/plan.md): **the chat UI.** Dark glass with Roboto. It talks **only** to our API (requirement 6). Visuals are chosen by code from the tool results, and only where they show something the text can't.

![A conversation: Dallas score breakdown, Miami vs Houston grid, Denver seasonality, Seattle premise correction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yardenfarag/Home-Assignment-Moveo/step-6-ui/docs/screenshots/desktop-conversation.png)

```text
<ProphetApp>  (src/app/_components/ProphetApp.tsx, "use client")
  useSyncExternalStore(units, sessionIds)        # this browser's settings + chat ids (localStorage)
  useChat(DefaultChatTransport → POST /api/chat)  # body: { sessionId, message, units } per sendMessage
  <Header>       wordmark · freshness · US/Metric · New chat
  <SideNav>      GET /api/chat/sessions?ids=…   → open: GET /api/chat/history?sessionId=…
  <main>
    <EmptyState>     the brief's four questions
    <AssistantMessage>
      streaming:  <ProgressList> (data-progress) · text deltas · "Double-checking…" (data-retry)
      final:      <FinalAnswerCard> (data-answer)
                    <PremiseBanner> · <Markdown> · pickVisuals(answer) → visuals
                    <RecommendationBox> · confidence · <Disclosure>×2 · follow-up chips
      failed:     <ErrorCard> (data-error: message + hint + Try again)
    <Composer>   Enter sends · Shift+Enter newline · Stop
  <WidgetsRail>  GET /api/widgets — phone: swipe strip · tablet: row · desktop: column
  <Footer>       Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0) · FEMA attribution
```

| Visual (U3b) | Shows what text can't | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Score breakdown** | *where* a hub's score comes from: each hazard's points + the worst-hazard boost | `explain_hub_score.formula.contributions` |
| **Comparison grid** | hubs × hazards at a glance, level color **and** text | `compare_hubs` |
| **Seasonality strip** | *when* hazard days happen (month by month) | `get_weather_stat.byMonth` |
| **Ranked list** | the ranking itself (no chart) | `rank_hubs` |

## Decisions (D80–D88, round U1–U8)

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D80 | Layout: chats · chat · overview. Phone swipe strip, tablet row, desktop column |
| D81 | Answer card anatomy. Only the **validated** answer gets the data panel |
| D82 | **Visuals only where they add value.** Recharts dropped, pure HTML/CSS |
| D83 | Tools return dual-unit thresholds, monthly counts and score contributions (code-computed) |
| D84 | Chat history = **this browser's chats only**. Refresh = new chat. Retry feedback hidden |
| D85 | `@ai-sdk/react` 4.0.186 (pins our `ai` 7.0.181), `react-markdown` |
| D86 | Accessibility (aria-live, keyboard, focus, reduced motion, text with every color). Light personality (cat, owl) |
| D87 | The UI imports tool **output types** from exported tool functions, so shapes aren't duplicated |
| D88 | Prompt rule: no Markdown tables (the UI draws grids) |

## Evidence

**Tests:** `Test Files 34 passed · Tests 163 passed`. Type check, lint and build are clean. New tests cover:
- monthly counts
- transcript pairing (hides retry feedback, drops unanswered questions)
- the visual picker (skips failed and duplicate calls, puts the most useful first, caps at 2)

**Driven like a real user.** Headless Chrome via the DevTools protocol (no new dependency) sends the login on every request, types questions, clicks Ask, waits, and takes screenshots:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Desktop, 4 brief-style questions in one chat | Each answered in 12–16 s. Dallas: "✓ Checked against the data" + breakdown. Miami/Houston: grid. Denver: 9% measurable / 4.7% scored + seasonality strips. Seattle: **"Heads-up: Seattle's hurricane risk isn't High — the data says Low"** + Medium confidence explained |
| Tablet (1100 px) | Overview as a row of three above the chat |
| Phone (390 px) | Overview as a swipe strip, chat right below |

**Bugs found by looking at the screenshots, all fixed:**
1. The side nav didn't show a new chat. A session gets its title only when its first answer is saved, so the nav now refreshes after each answer.
2. The model wrote a Markdown **table**, which rendered as raw pipes and duplicated the grid. Fixed with D88.
3. **Seasonality bars were flat.** Percentage heights had no definite parent, so the layout was restructured.
4. **The phone page was wider than the screen.** The swipe strip stretched the grid column. Fixed with `minmax(0,1fr)` + `min-w-0`, lesson #15.
5. The composer background was too see-through, because `.glass` sat outside Tailwind's layers and beat utility classes. Fixed by moving it into `@layer components`, lesson #16.
6. A leftover server from Step 5 was still serving the old build on the test port. Lesson #17.
7. Code review fixes: React lint caught refs read during render and setState in an effect. Now `useSyncExternalStore` + request body via `sendMessage`. Two single-source-of-truth slips were fixed (composer char limit, retry prefix).

Screenshots are in `docs/screenshots/` and the README now shows the conversation shot.

**Session log:** refreshed after the `CRON_SECRET` rotation, and the leak check passed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

UI and read-only endpoints. The tool output changes are additive (new fields).

**Blast Radius:** small

`/` is now the full app (still behind the login).

## Env vars

None new.

## Next: Step 7 (evals)

13 cases + `npm run eval`, plus a re-check of D57 (flood) and the over-exploring tool calls.

content.text:
**[PR #7](https://github.com/yardenfarag/Home-Assignment-Moveo/pull/7) is open: the chat UI is built.** I tested it by driving the real app in a headless browser on desktop, tablet and phone. A screenshot of a full conversation is embedded in the PR and in the README. 163 tests pass.

**What it does:**
- **Live progress** while the agent works ("Breaking down Dallas's risk score…"), then the answer appears as it's written.
- **Visuals only where they add something the text can't** (your U3 point):
  - **Score breakdown:** where a hub's score comes from.
  - **Comparison grid:** hubs × hazards at a glance.
  - **Seasonality strip:** *when* hazard days happen. For example, Denver's snow falls January–April and November–December.
  - **Rankings:** a clean list, no chart.

  The chart library is gone entirely; these are plain HTML/CSS.
- **Honesty is visible:**
  - an amber *"Heads-up: Seattle's hurricane risk isn't High — the data says Low"* banner
  - "✓ Checked against the data" when the question's assumption holds
  - the reason behind a Medium-confidence rating
  - "How I got this", which also says if any number in the text couldn't be traced to the data
- **Chat history** in a side nav, showing this browser's chats only. Refreshing starts a new chat, and old chats reopen exactly as they were answered.
- **US/Metric switch**, friendly errors with a "Try again" button, keyboard and screen-reader support, and the 🐱 and 🦉 touches.

**Seven problems found and fixed**, details in the PR. Five were visible only in the screenshots:
- new chats not appearing in the side nav
- the model writing a table that showed as raw `|` characters
- flat seasonality bars
- the phone page being wider than the screen
- a see-through composer

The other two:
- a leftover test server that was still serving the old build
- two React patterns flagged by the linter

I've added four new hard-won lessons (#15–#18) to `CLAUDE.md`.

**To try it yourself before merging:**
```bash
git checkout step-6-ui
npm run build
npm start          # http://localhost:3000, then sign in with APP_USERNAME / APP_PASSWORD
```

**Next is Step 7, the evals:** a 13-question test set run with `npm run eval`, which prints pass/fail per case. Expected answers are computed from the live data at run time, never typed in by hand. As we agreed, this is also where I'll re-check two things: the flood scores that max out (D57), and the model calling more tools than it needs. No new `.env` values needed. When you merge, I'll start with a short round on the exact pass/fail checks.

feedback:
-i think we should change the name of the project to Sneakoscope, its better for the purpose of the tool. change it everywhere.
-the giant cat in the desktop - i think its not a good fit, lets remove it and come up with an icon svg of our own.
-'which hubs should we protect today' sounds a bit commercialized, lets use more natural language.
-widgets on the side are not very clear.. what do they mean? why is this important?

Good feedback, all four points. My plan for each:

1. **Rename to Sneakoscope everywhere:** UI, metadata, agent instructions, error text, login prompt, code names, package name and docs. One exception: the session log stays as it was recorded, since it's a historical record. The README will note the rename.
2. **The cat goes.** I'll draw an original Sneakoscope icon as SVG (a glass spinning top with a soft inner glow) and use it as the logo and empty-state art.
3. **Natural headline**, instead of "Which hubs should we protect first?".
4. **Clearer widgets:** each panel gets a plain title, a one-line explanation of what it shows and why it matters, and the Low/Medium/High scale. All built from the config, so the numbers can't drift.

Ask in plain language. Every number comes from deterministic, tested code, and the agent says when the data is unsure.
-| D1 | Name: **The Daily Prophet**. Original design, no Harry Potter logos, fonts, crests or characters. | Fun theme without copying anyone's brand. |
+| D1 | Name: **Sneakoscope**. Original design, no Harry Potter logos, fonts, crests or characters. | Fun theme without copying anyone's brand. |
| D2 | **36 hubs**, one per major US metro, stored as rows in the database. Adding a city = adding a row. | The brief asked for 25–50 metros and for hubs to be data, not code. |
| D3 | "Midwest", "South" and so on use the **official US Census regions**. | Gives "Which Midwest hubs…" a clear, quotable definition. |

| D4 | A hub's location is the **city-center point**. FEMA data comes from the county that point is in. | Simple and consistent. A real warehouse can sit elsewhere in the metro (written down as an assumption). |
Agreed on 2026-11-25 after a structured "grilling" session (see `docs/session/`).
Every individual choice and its reason is in [decisions.md](decisions.md).

All your review points are done and pushed to **[PR #7](https://github.com/yardenfarag/Home-Assignment-Moveo/pull/7)**. I updated the PR title and posted a summary comment there. 163 tests pass and the build is clean.

**What changed:**
- **Renamed to Sneakoscope everywhere:** the UI, browser tab, the agent's introduction, error messages, the login prompt, the code and the docs. Three things keep the old name on purpose:
  - the session log, since it's a historical record
  - the comment in the first database migration, for the same reason
  - the Supabase project name `daily-prophet`, which our tools can't rename. It's only a label in the dashboard; rename it there if you'd like.
- **New icon, drawn from scratch:** a glass spinning top with a glowing amber core, since a Sneakoscope "lights up when something's wrong". It's the header logo, the empty-state art (with a gentle glow) and the browser-tab icon. The big cat is gone.
- **Your wording, word for word:** "Weather risk across our hubs / Ask me about weather risk across our 36 hubs…". The only change is that "36" comes from the live data, so adding a city updates it automatically.
- **Widgets that explain themselves.** Each panel has a plain title, one line on what it shows and why it matters, the Low/Medium/High scale, and a hint that you can click any row:
  - **Most at-risk hubs:** the first places to look at for resilience upgrades.
  - **Most exposed hub, per hazard:** useful when an upgrade targets one hazard, like flood barriers.
  - **About the data:** how current the numbers are and where they come from.
- **"New chat" only in the chat list.** The header button is gone. On phones it's under ☰.
- **Hub names no longer cut off** in the per-hazard panel (I removed a redundant "/100").

Two small things for you to decide:
1. **"with a confidence level on every answer" is almost always true, but not quite.** Off-topic replies ("I only cover weather risk…") don't get a confidence level, because there's no data behind them. Keep the line as is, or change it to "on every data answer"? I'd keep it; the exception is minor and obvious.
2. **Two small emojis remain in error messages:** 🐱 in "Today's weather data hasn't landed yet" and 😿 in "Something went wrong on our side". Keep them, or remove them too for a fully professional tone?

Once PR #7 is merged, next is **Step 7, the evals.**

Hubs scored
36 - is it an average?

No, it's not an average. It's a **count**: 36 hubs got a score in the latest nightly run, which is all of our hubs. Since it sits next to scores, it's easy to misread as a score itself, so the label isn't doing its job.

I'd rename it to **"Hubs tracked: 36"**. Alternatively, "Hubs covered: 36 of 36" would also show if any hub failed to score in a run.

Want me to make that change in PR #7? Which wording do you prefer?

content.text:
## Step 7: evals, question round

❓ **E1** - **How the evals run:**
- **Default mode:** `npm run eval` runs the **real agent in-process**: real model, real database, the same code path as `/api/chat`, but **nothing gets saved** as chat history (eval runs shouldn't fill your side nav). Multi-turn cases keep their history in memory.
- **`--url` mode:** `npm run eval -- --url=https://…` sends the same cases to a **deployed** `/api/chat` and reads the stream. We'll use it in Step 10 to test the live site.

Both modes share the same case list and checks.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **E2** - **Expected values are computed when the eval runs, never typed in by hand** (Q18). Each case has a small "oracle" that asks the scoring and stats code for the right answer at that moment: the top Midwest winter hub, Denver's % of days with measurable snow in 2025, Dallas's real level. So the evals stay correct after tonight's re-score.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **E3** - **The 13 cases.** *Hard* checks decide pass/fail:

| # | Question | Hard checks |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Midwest hubs most exposed to winter? | `rank_hubs` (winter, Midwest); the **first hub named** = computed #1 |
| 2 | Compare Miami & Houston, hurricane + flood | `compare_hubs` with both; Miami hurricane + Houston flood **numbers match** the snapshot |
| 3 | % of Denver days last year with snowfall | `get_weather_stat` (measurable snow, **2025**); the **% matches** what code computes |
| 4 | Why is Dallas's risk high? | `explain_hub_score(dallas)`; the premise verdict matches Dallas's real level |
| 5 | Why is Seattle's hurricane risk so high? | premise flagged as **wrong** (`holds: false`) |
| 6 | Follow-up: "…Midwest winter?" → "Why that one?" | turn 2 explains the **computed #1 hub** |
| 7 | Top 5 hubs overall | the 5 hubs named = the computed top 5 |
| 8 | What about Boise? | no Boise numbers; says it's **not one of our hubs** |
| 9 | Dust storm risk in Phoenix? | says dust storms **aren't scored** |
| 10 | Prioritize Houston or Denver? | recommendation + disclaimer present, backed by data |
| 11 | Write me a poem | `outOfScope: true`, 0 tools |
| 12 | Heavy-rain days in Houston last year | the period used is **calendar 2025**, and the answer says so |
| 13 | How sure are you about Seattle's winter score? | confidence = the computed Medium, and it explains the disagreement |

On **every** case, an answer must be produced, i.e. it passed the number checks within one retry.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **E4** - **Soft metrics: reported, not pass/fail.** Per case and in total:
- number of tool calls, plus **duplicate calls**, which is the "over-exploring" issue from Step 4
- numbers in the text that couldn't be traced to the data
- retries
- time per answer
- tokens and **estimated cost**

These are what the Step 8 model bakeoff compares, after accuracy.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **E5** - **Cost and repeats.** One run of all 13 on Sonnet ≈ **$1**, about 4 minutes. An optional `--repeat=3` checks *consistency*, since model answers vary; that costs about $3. The default is 1 run.

➡️ Yes: default 1, use `--repeat=3` for the bakeoff.

---

❓ **E6** - **Where results go.** The terminal shows a clear table (✅/❌ per case and check, soft metrics, then the total) and the exit code is 1 if anything fails. Each run also saves a JSON report to `evals/results/`, which is gitignored. The **latest summary is committed** as `docs/evals.md`, so reviewers can see real results.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **E7** - **The D57 flood check (S10), honestly:** an eval can check that the agent *repeats* our flood scores correctly, but not whether the scores are *sensible*. That's a judgment call. So the eval will also print a **flood top 10, with each hub's observed and FEMA halves side by side**, and we look at it together and decide whether D57 needs action.

➡️ Yes.

---

**The three open UI questions** (small, and they can ride along in this PR):

❓ **H1** - Rename "Hubs scored: 36" to **"Hubs tracked: 36"**. ➡️ Yes.

❓ **H2** - Keep your line "…with a confidence level on every answer" as is. Off-topic replies don't get one, which is an obvious exception. ➡️ Keep it.

❓ **H3** - The two small emojis in error messages (🐱 "data hasn't landed yet", 😿 "something went wrong"): keep or remove? ➡️ **Remove**, to match the professional tone you set when removing the big cat. Your call.

No new `.env` values for this step.

content.text:
All green: 167 tests pass. With the method facts derived from config, the 7 "untraced" warnings from this run would all clear.

The run surfaced two things that are your call. Here's the evidence.

---

❓ **E8** - **Duplicate tool calls: 6 in this run.** The agent sometimes calls the *same* tool with the *same* input more than once in one answer:

| Case | Duplicate calls |
|---|---|
| Dallas | `explain_hub_score(dallas)` ×4 |
| Seattle (false premise) | `explain_hub_score(seattle)` ×2 |
| Midwest | `rank_hubs(winter, Midwest)` ×2 |
| Confidence | `get_weather_stat(seattle, snow_day…)` ×2 |

It's harmless to correctness, since all 13 cases passed. But each duplicate resends the **whole** result into the conversation, and the explain result is the biggest one, so it inflates tokens and cost. My prompt rule ("never call the same tool twice with the same input") clearly isn't enough.

**Proposal:** handle it in code. When a call repeats one already made in the same answer, the tool returns a tiny reply ("Same as an earlier call in this answer — use that result.") instead of re-sending the full data. The ledger, the checks and the visuals are unaffected, because the first result is already recorded. Then I re-run the evals to show the token difference.

➡️ Yes: dedupe in code, then measure.

---

❓ **E9** - **The D57 flood review.** Here's the top 10 by flood score, with both halves:

| Hub | Flood | Observed half (heavy-rain days/yr) | FEMA half (inland · coastal events/yr) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Houston | 84.0 | 68 (3.4) | **100** (5.14 · 3.76) |
| Dallas | 78.0 | 56 (2.8) | **100** (4.61 · n/a) |
| Miami | 76.0 | 52 (2.6) | **100** (4.00 · 2.25) |
| Los Angeles | 74.0 | 48 (2.4) | **100** (3.96 · 2.17) |
| New Orleans | 72.2 | 68 (3.4) | 76.3 (2.68 · 3.75) |
| Memphis | 72.0 | 44 (2.2) | **100** (5.18 · n/a) |
| Boston | 68.0 | 36 (1.8) | **100** (1.68 · 7.40) |
| Nashville · Kansas City · Charlotte | 68 · 62 · 61.5 | 36 · 24 · 24 | **100 · 100 · 99** |

What the table shows:
- **The FEMA half is maxed out at 100 for 9 of the top 10.** So within this group, the flood ranking is effectively driven by **observed heavy-rain days** alone.
- **County size distorts the one FEMA value that isn't maxed out.** New Orleans gets the *lowest* FEMA flood value of the group (76.3), not because it floods less (it's famously flood-prone), but because **Orleans Parish is a small county**, so it logs fewer flood warning-days.
- **The ranking still holds up broadly.** Houston at #1 (Harvey) is very defensible. **Los Angeles at #4 is the most questionable**, since it's inflated by a huge county (4,797 sq mi).

Options:
- **(a) Keep v1.** Close D57 as "reviewed, kept", with the limitation stated plainly in the docs. The agent already tells users this in its flood caveat.
- **(b) Score inland flood per county area**, like tornado (D53). This lowers LA and Harris and raises small counties like New Orleans. It needs new national anchors, a scoring-version bump to **v2**, a re-score and fresh evals: about 30–45 minutes.

➡️ **(a) for now**, listing (b) as the first scoring improvement after deploy. The flood score's main weakness is already disclosed to users, and Steps 8–10 (bakeoff, docs, deploy) matter more for the deadline.

e8-yes
e9-ok

Both agreed. **E8 (dedupe)** first, test-first. Tool calls made *in parallel* within one step start at the same moment, so the check has to "claim" a call **when it starts**, not when it finishes; otherwise both parallel copies would run:

Confirmed. Both are the model **doing its own arithmetic**:
- *"4.3 points between 1st and 5th"* is 73.9 − 69.6
- *"The gap is 11.2 points"* is 69.1 (Houston) − 57.9 (Denver)

The math happens to be right, but it breaks our rule that **the LLM never produces numbers**, and the soft check caught it as designed. (The "9" turned out to be a stray digit match, not a real figure.) Gaps are genuinely useful to an analyst, though, so banning them would make answers worse. One question:

❓ **E10** - **Give the model code-computed gaps, and stop retries from triggering re-calls:**
1. `rank_hubs` also returns **`spread`** (first minus last score in the list), and `compare_hubs` returns **`differences`** (hub A minus hub B, for overall and each hazard). Both are computed in code, so the model can say "4.3 points apart" with a **checked** number.
2. A prompt line: *"Never compute differences, ratios or averages yourself; use the gaps the tools provide."*
3. A wording fix in the retry message: replace "call more tools if needed" with *"use the tool results you already have; only call a tool if you truly need new data"*. That's what caused most of Dallas's repeats.

Then a final `--publish` eval run.

Both exist and are cheap, with structured output:
- **Luna:** `openai/gpt-6-luna`, $0.10 / $0.50 per 1M tokens

E10 is approved, and I'll build it together with the judge. A few judge decisions first, because *where* it runs changes cost and speed for your users:

---

❓ **J1** - **Where the judge runs:**
- **(a) In the evals only.** It grades every eval answer offline. Zero cost or delay for real users.
- **(b) On every live answer, blocking.** Users wait about 2–4 s more per answer, and a judge "fail" triggers a retry. The catch: a cheap judge can be wrong too, so it could block *good* answers. Our code checks already guarantee the numbers.
- **(c) On every live answer, non-blocking.** The answer shows immediately, then the judge runs in the background and the card gets a small "✓ Reviewed" or "⚠ Flagged for review" badge, with every verdict logged to `events`.

➡️ **(a) now + (c) after deploy.** The evals prove the judge is reliable *first*, then we expose it to users without slowing anyone down.

---

❓ **J2** - **Judge model:** `openai/gpt-6-luna`, set in a new `JUDGE_MODEL` env var with the same OpenRouter key.
- It's a **different provider** from the answering model (Claude), which avoids a model grading its own style too kindly.
- The cost is about **$0.001 per graded answer**.
- Qwen 3.8 Flash is the fallback option.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **J3** - **What the judge checks.** It gets the question, the answer, the premise verdict and **the actual tool results**, and returns structured scores from 1 to 5:

| Criterion | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| **Faithful to data** | Is every claim supported by the tool results? Lists any unsupported claims. |
| **Answers the question** | Does it address what was actually asked? |
| **Honest about limits** | Does it state relevant uncertainty, without overclaiming? |
| **Premise handling** | If the question assumed something wrong, does the answer correct it up front? |
| **Clarity** | Could an analyst act on it? |

**Hard check:** faithful ≥ 4 *and* the judge's overall verdict is pass. The other scores are reported as soft metrics. Judges are noisy, so only the most important criterion is pass/fail.

➡️ Yes.

---

❓ **J4** - **Test the judge itself.** Each eval run includes **2 deliberately bad answers**: one with a wrong number, one that agrees with a false premise. If the judge doesn't fail both, the report says the **judge is unreliable** and its verdicts shouldn't be trusted. That's the only way to know the extra validation actually validates.

➡️ Yes.

---

New env var: `JUDGE_MODEL=openai/gpt-6-luna`. I'll add it to `.env.local` and `.env.example`; there's no new key.

### Evals (Step 7, round E1–E9)
| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D94 | **`npm run eval`**: 13 cases (the brief's 4 questions + premise pushback, follow-up, top 5, unknown city, unscored hazard, decision, off-topic, "last year", confidence). Each has **hard checks** (the right tool with the right input, the right top hub, numbers matching the data, the premise verdict) and **soft metrics** (tool calls, duplicates, untraced numbers, retries, latency, tokens, cost). Expected values come from an **oracle** built on the same core functions at run time (E2). In-process by default, with **nothing saved to chat history**. `--url` hits a deployed `/api/chat`. `--repeat`, `--model`, `--case`, `--publish` (writes `docs/evals.md`). Reports go to `evals/results/` (gitignored). An `eval.finished` event is logged. (E1–E6) | Concrete, repeatable checks that stay correct after every nightly re-score. The soft metrics feed the Step 8 bakeoff. |
| D95 | **Method facts count as "known numbers"** in the free-text check: level cut-offs, formula weights, hazard weights, the 50/50 blend, the scoring window, thresholds in both unit systems (all derived from config) and the live hub count. | The first eval run flagged 7 "untraced" numbers. All 7 were method facts the agent quotes from its instructions (67, 0.6, 0.4, 50%, 36, 0.4 in), not invented data. |
| D96 | **Duplicate tool calls are handled in code** (E8): a repeat of an identical call in the same answer (including parallel repeats) returns a short "same as an earlier call" reply instead of re-running and re-sending the full result. It's still recorded, so the eval still counts it. | The first run had 6 duplicates (Dallas: `explain_hub_score` ×4). The prompt rule alone didn't stop them, and each duplicate re-sent the largest tool result. |
| D97 | **D57 reviewed and kept for v1** (E9). The FEMA flood half is at 100 for 9 of the top 10 flood hubs, so flood rankings are effectively driven by observed heavy-rain days. County size distorts the rest (small Orleans Parish → New Orleans gets the lowest FEMA value of the group; huge LA County → Los Angeles is ranked #4). **First scoring improvement after deploy:** score inland flood per county area, like tornado (D53), as scoring v2. | The order is still broadly defensible (Houston #1), and the agent already states the limitation. Bakeoff, docs and deploy matter more for the deadline. |
| D88 | **No Markdown tables in answers** (prompt rule). The UI draws grids from the data. | A model-written table rendered as raw pipes, and it duplicated the comparison grid. |


## Engineering

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D31 | **One Next.js app** with `src/core/` free of Next.js and React, **enforced by an ESLint rule**. (Q1) | Core logic can be tested and run from scripts and evals without the web framework. Simpler than a monorepo. |
| D32 | Supabase project **`daily-prophet` in us-east-1**, close to Vercel's default region. (Q2) | Low latency between the app and the DB. |
| D33 | **RLS on every table with no policies.** Only the server (secret key) can read or write. The browser never talks to the DB. | Nothing is exposed even if the public key leaks. |
| D34 | **Every table has `created_at` + `updated_at`** (a trigger keeps `updated_at` current), plus an **`events`** table that replaces a separate `ingest_runs` table. | Your standing rule: be able to track and analyze everything. One events table covers runs, failures, retries and guard decisions. |
| D35 | Errors at boundaries use **`ErrorName \|\| message \|\| function \|\| emoji`**, with a fixed emoji per boundary: 🦉 LLM, 🐸 Open-Meteo, 🦡 FEMA, 🐘 database, 🦄 API route, 🐍 Jev, 🦔 config. Users only see a clean `{error:{code,message}}`. (Q17) | Your format. A fixed emoji makes logs searchable by origin. |
| D36 | Hub IDs are **readable slugs** (`kansas-city`), not airport codes. | Clearer for the LLM, logs and humans. |
| D37 | **Tailwind CSS** for styling (it ships with the Next.js starter). | Fast to build the glass UI, and no extra dependency. |
| D38 | The hub seed is a **SQL migration**. Migrations are applied through the Supabase connection and also saved in `supabase/migrations/`. | The database can be rebuilt from the repo. |
| D39 | `@types/node` bumped to **v22** to match Node 22 (Vitest 5 requires it). | Fixes the install conflict. Matches the runtime. |
| D40 | **PR per step.** Claude opens it, Yarden reviews and merges. Claude never pushes to `main` (except the single empty initial commit an empty repo needs as a PR base). (Q3) | Review before anything lands. |
| D41 | The session log is exported to `docs/session/` with **private details scrubbed** (emails, keys, home path, login codes). The model's private reasoning blocks and internal bookkeeping records are left out. (Q4) | The assignment requires the full session, and the repo is public. |
| D42 | **Project rules live in `CLAUDE.md`** (auto-read by Claude Code). Its first line `@AGENTS.md` pulls in the Next.js notice without copying it. (R5) | One place for how we work. Committed so reviewers can see the process. |
| D43 | **Decide together:** Claude asks before anything that changes product behavior, data, architecture, dependencies, schema, scoring or UX. Mechanical things get done and logged. (R7) | We're a team. Earlier, D36–D39 and D14a–c were decided by Claude without asking first. |
| D44 | **Errors are caught at boundaries; pure functions throw plain errors.** This clarifies "always try/catch". (R1) | Avoids swallowed or triple-wrapped errors while keeping the unified format. |
| D45 | **Every external call has a timeout, including Supabase** (wrapped `fetch`, landing with Step 2). (R2) | Writing the rule exposed that Supabase calls had no timeout and could hang forever. |
| D46 | **Mirrored facts get drift tests:** event sources and Census regions vs DB constraints, env schemas vs `.env.example`. Docs link to the scoring config instead of restating the numbers. (R3) | Single source of truth. Where a copy is unavoidable, drift fails a test instead of going unnoticed. |

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D31 | **One Next.js app** with `src/core/` free of Next.js and React, **enforced by an ESLint rule**. (Q1) | Core logic can be tested and run from scripts and evals without the web framework. Simpler than a monorepo. |
| D32 | Supabase project **`daily-prophet` in us-east-1**, close to Vercel's default region. (Q2) | Low latency between the app and the DB. |
| D33 | **RLS on every table with no policies.** Only the server (secret key) can read or write. The browser never talks to the DB. | Nothing is exposed even if the public key leaks. |

Users only see a clean `{error:{code,message}}`. (Q17) | Your format. A fixed emoji makes logs searchable by origin. |
| D36 | Hub IDs are **readable slugs** (`kansas-city`), not airport codes. | Clearer for the LLM, logs and humans. |
| D37 | **Tailwind CSS** for styling (it ships with the Next.js starter). | Fast to build the glass UI, and no extra dependency. |
| D38 | The hub seed is a **SQL migration**. Migrations are applied through the Supabase connection and also saved in `supabase/migrations/`. | The database can be rebuilt from the repo. |
| D39 | `@types/node` bumped to **v22** to match Node 22 (Vitest 5 requires it). | Fixes the install conflict. Matches the runtime. |
| D40 | **PR per step.** Claude opens it, Yarden reviews and merges. Claude never pushes to `main` (except the single empty initial commit an empty repo needs as a PR base). (Q3) | Review before anything lands. |
| D41 | The session log is exported to `docs/session/` with **private details scrubbed** (emails, keys, home path, login codes). The model's private reasoning blocks and internal bookkeeping records are left out. (Q4) | The assignment requires the full session, and the repo is public. |
| D42 | **Project rules live in `CLAUDE.md`** (auto-read by Claude Code). Its first line `@AGENTS.md` pulls in the Next.js notice without copying it. (R5) | One place for how we work. Committed so reviewers can see the process. |
| D43 | **Decide together:** Claude asks before anything that changes product behavior, data, architecture, dependencies, schema, scoring or UX. Mechanical things get done and logged. (R7) | We're a team. Earlier, D36–D39 and D14a–c were decided by Claude without asking first. |
| D44 | **Errors are caught at boundaries; pure functions throw plain errors.** This clarifies "always try/catch". (R1) | Avoids swallowed or triple-wrapped errors while keeping the unified format. |
| D45 | **Every external call has a timeout, including Supabase** (wrapped `fetch`, landing with Step 2). (R2) | Writing the rule exposed that Supabase calls had no timeout and could hang forever. |
| D46 | **Mirrored facts get drift tests:** event sources and Census regions vs DB constraints, env schemas vs `.env.example`. Docs link to the scoring config instead of restating the numbers. (R3) | Single source of truth. Where a copy is unavoidable, drift fails a test instead of going unnoticed. |

Analysts chat with it to find out which hubs are most exposed to severe weather, compare hubs, and understand *why* a hub is risky, to help decide where to invest in resilience upgrades. > 🚧 Work in progress. Built step by step. See [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md). ## Docs - [Plan](docs/plan.md): architecture, tables, steps - [Decision log](docs/decisions.md): every choice and why - [Assumptions, uncertainty & scope](docs/assumptions.md) - [Design](docs/design.md) - [AI session log](docs/session/): the full conversation with the coding agent ## Run locally Requirements: Node 22+, a Supabase project. ```bash npm install cp .env.example .env.local # then fill in the values (see comments in the file) npm run db:check # verifies the database connection: lists the hubs npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 ``` ## Scripts | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `npm run dev` | Start the app locally | | `npm test` | Unit tests (Vitest) | | `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check | | `npm run lint` | ESLint (includes the rule keeping `src/core` free of Next.js) | | `npm run db:check` | Connect to Supabase and list hubs per region | | `npm run ingest` | Fetch FEMA + Open-Meteo data for all active hubs (incremental; the first full load takes about 1 h because of Open-Meteo's rate limits) | | `npm run ingest -- --hub=dallas,denver` | Same, for selected hubs only | | `npm run ingest -- --refresh-fema` | Re-fetch FEMA records for every hub (e.g. after a new NRI release) | | `npm run score` | Re-score all hubs from stored data (no API calls). The ingest runs this automatically. | | `npm run ask -- "question"` | Ask the real agent from the terminal (add `--session=` for a follow-up, `--metric` for metric units) | | `npm run fema:anchors` | Recompute the national 95th-percentile FEMA anchors (for review before changing `scoring/config.ts`) | | `npm run session:export -- ` | Export the AI session log to `docs/session/` (scrubbed) | ## The app ![Sneakoscope: a conversation with score breakdowns, a comparison grid, seasonality strips and a premise correction](docs/screenshots/desktop-conversation.png) More screenshots: [start screen](docs/screenshots/desktop-start.png) · [phone](docs/screenshots/phone-start.png). Ask in plain language. Every number comes from deterministic, tested code, and the agent says when the data is unsure. Use the **US / Metric** switch to change units, and the side nav to reopen this browser's earlier chats. ## API Every route requires the site login (HTTP Basic Auth: `APP_USERNAME` / `APP_PASSWORD`), except the cron route. | Route | What it does | |---|---| | `POST /api/chat` | Body `{ "sessionId": null \| "", "message": "…", "units": "us" \| "metric" }`. Streams the AI SDK chat protocol: `data-session`, `data-progress`, answer text, then `data-answer` (validated) or `data-error`. | | `GET /api/widgets` | Top 5 hubs, the leading hub per hazard, data freshness. | | `GET /api/cron/ingest` | Nightly job (Vercel Cron, 06:00 UTC): fetch new weather, then re-score. Needs `Authorization: Bearer `. | Errors are always friendly JSON: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "hint", "retryable" } }`. ```bash curl -u "$APP_USERNAME:$APP_PASSWORD" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"sessionId":null,"message":"Which Midwest hubs are most exposed to winter?","units":"us"}' \ http://localhost:3000/api/chat ``` ## Evals ```bash npm run eval # 13 cases on OPENROUTER_MODEL, about 3 min, about $1 on Sonnet npm run eval -- --model=openai/gpt-6.1-terra # try another model npm run eval -- --repeat=3 # consistency check npm run eval -- --url=https://your-app.vercel.app # test a deployment ``` Prints pass/fail per case and check, plus soft metrics (tool calls, duplicates, latency, tokens, cost), and exits 1 on failure. Expected values are computed from the live data at run time. Latest results: [docs/evals.md](docs/evals.md). ## Database SQL migrations live in [supabase/migrations/](supabase/migrations/). Apply them in order to a fresh Supabase project (SQL editor or Supabase CLI). # 🦉 Sneakoscope — Plan

Agreed on 2026-11-25 after a structured "grilling" session (see `docs/session/`).
Every individual choice and its reason is in [decisions.md](decisions.md).

## Goal
A chat agent that helps logistics analysts decide which distribution hubs are most
exposed to severe weather and should get resilience investment. It ranks, compares
and explains hubs using **deterministic, tested scoring code**. The LLM only chooses
tools and explains their results. It never invents numbers.

## Architecture (target)
```
Browser (Next.js UI: Roboto, dark glass)
  │  POST /api/chat {sessionId, message}  → streams progress + text + validated answer
  │  GET  /api/widgets                    → top hubs, hazard leaders, data status
  ▼
proxy.ts — Basic Auth on everything except /api/cron/* (uses CRON_SECRET)
  ▼
src/app/api/*  (thin: Zod-parse → call core → format response/errors)
  ▼
src/core/  (no Next.js; testable alone)
  agent/   AI SDK v7 streamText + 4 tools + Output.object(answer schema)
           → validate → code overrides confidence/disclaimer → retry once → error
  tools/   rank_hubs · compare_hubs · get_weather_stat · explain_hub_score
  scoring/ pure: thresholds → per-hazard 0–100 → overall → level → confidence
  stats/   pure: counts / % / ranges over daily rows
  ingest/  incremental: Open-Meteo + FEMA → DB → scoring → nightly snapshot
  db/      Supabase repositories (server-only secret key)
  ▼                    ▼                          ▼
Supabase Postgres   OpenRouter (LLM + Jev)   Open-Meteo archive · FEMA NRI ArcGIS
        ▲
Vercel Cron (daily) → /api/cron/ingest      npm run ingest (first full load, local)
```

## Database tables
Every table has `created_at` + `updated_at` (trigger-maintained). RLS on, no public policies.

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `hubs` | id slug, name, state, Census region, lat/lon, timezone, county FIPS/name, active |
| `weather_daily` | hub × date: snowfall, min temp, precipitation, max gust, max apparent temp |
| `fema_nri` | per hub: NRI version + annualized frequency per hazard + raw record |
| `score_snapshots` | per hub per ingest run: overall, level, top hazard, breakdown, confidence, window, scoring_version |
| `chat_sessions`, `chat_messages` | server-side conversation memory incl. tool results |
| `events` | append-only log (ingest, scoring, validation failures, retries, guard decisions, errors), grouped by `correlation_id` |

## Scoring (summary)
- 6 hazards and weights: hurricane 25%, winter 20%, flood/rain 20%, severe storms (tornado + hail) 15%, wind 10%, heat 10%.
- Each hazard is scored 0–100 on a fixed absolute scale. Mixed hazards are 50% observed (Open-Meteo) + 50% FEMA annualized frequency.
- Overall = 60% weighted average + 40% highest hazard. Levels: Low 0–33, Medium 34–66, High 67–100.
- Confidence (High/Medium/Low) is computed in code from data completeness and the number of sources.
- Rolling 5-year window ending at the newest available day. The relative rank among hubs is shown next to the score.

## Steps (one branch + PR each; Yarden merges)
| # | Step | New env vars |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Supabase project, scaffold, lint boundary, Vitest, env validation, error helper, schema + events, 36-hub seed, docs, session export | `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` |
| 2 | Open-Meteo + FEMA clients, incremental paced ingest, first full load, check wind-gust distribution | — |
| 3 | Anchor values reviewed with real data → scoring test-first → snapshots | — |
| 4 | Agent: tools, answer schema + validation + retry, recommendation rules, chat history | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_MODEL` |
| 5 | Streaming `POST /api/chat`, `/api/widgets`, cron route, Basic Auth | `APP_USERNAME`, `APP_PASSWORD`, `CRON_SECRET` |
| 6 | UI: chat, 3 widgets, per-answer charts | — |
| 7 | Eval set (13 cases) + `npm run eval` (`--url` for deployed). **Revisit D57** (FEMA flood half capped for 15 hubs) if flood rankings look off | — |

I've added the judge, and the first full run says **6/13** cases pass. I don't think that number is trustworthy yet, and it isn't mainly the agent's fault. Two things to fix, one of which I've already done:

**1. The judge couldn't see what the agent saw (my bug, fixed).** It didn't get the agent's instructions (hub list, method facts) or, in follow-ups, the earlier turn's tool results. That's why it gave 1/5 for "Boise isn't one of our hubs" and 1/5 to a correct follow-up. Both are fixed and tested (178 tests, typecheck and lint clean).

**2. The pass/fail verdict is too noisy to fail a case on.** I graded the exact same 14 answers twice with the same evidence, at temperature 0:
- The **verdict flipped on 4 of 14** answers (Midwest, Miami vs Houston, Denver, last-year).
- The **faithful-to-data score held steady**: the only answers below 4 were the same in both passes.
- The self-test still caught **2/2** planted bad answers, so the judge does catch real errors.

**What it flags every time** (all three gradings):
- **Real agent issues worth fixing:**
  - Seattle ends with a guess: "if you saw something high, it was probably winter or flood." Both of those are Medium.
  - The follow-up says Detroit's score "leans on FEMA." The data doesn't show that.
- **General knowledge, not our data:**
  - "Gulf and Atlantic coasts" in the top-5 answer.
  - "Salt Lake City is the closest hub to Boise."
  - Background on dust storms and pointers to the NWS (National Weather Service) and ADOT (Arizona's transport department) as better sources.
  
  These are useful context, and none of them is a number. The judge can't verify them from tool results.

On the good side, E10 worked: **0 untraced numbers** (down from 3), **0 retries**, and 3 duplicate calls. Cost was $0.87.

**Questions:**
- **J5 – what the hard check needs:** **(rec)** faithful-to-data ≥ 4 only. The pass/fail verdict and the other four scores (answers the question, honest about limits, premise handling, clarity) become soft metrics. The current rule (verdict *pass* and faithful ≥ 4) fails cases on a coin flip.
- **J6 – general knowledge:** **(rec)** allow widely known context that isn't about our data (geography, what a haboob is, official warning sources). The agent must never present it as data. The judge lists these claims separately instead of counting them against faithfulness. The other option is to ban them in the agent's prompt, which makes answers less useful.
- **J7 – fix the two real issues in the system prompt:** no guessing about what the analyst may have seen, and only say a score "leans on" observed weather or FEMA when the tool's component scores show it. Then one full re-run (about $0.90) and publish. **(rec: yes)**
- **J8 – `--rejudge=<results.json>` flag:** re-grades saved answers without re-running the agent, for a few cents. That's how I ran the two re-gradings above, and it's handy for the Step 8 bakeoff. **(rec: yes)** Otherwise I'll delete the one-off script.

The docs for E10 (D98) and J1–J4 (D99–D102) are written. I'll adjust them to your answers, then export the session log and open PR #8. 🐱

return `You are Sneakoscope, a weather-risk analyst for a logistics company's US distribution hubs.
Analysts use you to decide which hubs to prioritize for resilience investment. Be clear, specific and honest.

# Today
Today is ${today}. "Last year" means calendar year ${year - 1}. "This year" means ${year} to date.

# Hard rules
1. NEVER state a number that a tool did not return. Never calculate, estimate, convert or round numbers yourself — copy them from tool results. Never compute differences, ratios or averages: use the "spread" and "gaps" values the tools provide. Every number you rely on goes into dataUsed.
2. Call a tool before ANY claim about a hub's score, rank, level or weather. Never answer from memory.
3. If the question ASSUMES something about a hub's level (e.g. "Why is Dallas high?", "Miami is low risk, right?"), first call explain_hub_score, set premiseClaim to what the question assumes, and if the data does not support it, say so plainly in the FIRST sentence before explaining.
4. Honesty over precision: when a result has medium or low confidence, say why using its confidenceReason. State the limits of the data. Never present a weak number as a fact.
5. We only cover the hubs listed below. If asked about another city, say it is not one of our hubs — do not guess.
6. If the question is not about weather risk for our hubs, set outOfScope=true, reply in one or two polite sentences about what you can help with, and call no tools.
7. For decision questions ("Should we invest in X or Y?") fill recommendation. Tie every reason to a number in dataUsed. Never sound certain — final decisions belong to the team.
8. Units: ${unitRule}
9. Answer first, then the reasons. Use short paragraphs or bullets in Markdown, at most ~250 words. No filler. Never write Markdown tables — the app draws comparison grids and charts from the tool results itself.
10. "Had snowfall" / "did it snow" questions: use the measurable_snow_day metric (the NWS bar for measurable snow), and ALSO report snow_day — the stricter level our winter score counts — so the analyst sees both.
11. Be efficient: 1-3 tool calls are usually enough. Never call the same tool twice with the same input — reuse the result you already have.

# How the risk score works (explain when asked; use tool numbers for specifics)
- Six hazards, each scored 0-100 on a fixed national scale: ${weights}.
- Mixed hazards blend 50% observed weather (Open-Meteo, last ${SCORING_WINDOW_DAYS} days) with 50% FEMA National Risk Index frequency. Hurricane and severe storms use FEMA only.
- Overall = ${OVERALL_MIX.weightedAverage} × weighted average + ${OVERALL_MIX.worstHazard} × worst hazard, so one severe hazard is not averaged away.
- Levels: Low 0-${RISK_LEVEL_CUTOFFS.mediumFrom - 1}, Medium ${RISK_LEVEL_CUTOFFS.mediumFrom}-${RISK_LEVEL_CUTOFFS.highFrom - 1}, High ${RISK_LEVEL_CUTOFFS.highFrom}-100.
- A "snow day" in our score is ${formatDual(snow, units)}.
- Confidence is computed by code from data completeness and whether the two sources agree.

# Our hubs (id: name, state (US Census region))
${hubList}`;
}

toolUseResult.originalFile: # Sneakoscope A weather risk intelligence agent for a logistics company's US distribution hubs. Analysts chat with it to find out which hubs are most exposed to severe weather, compare hubs, and understand *why* a hub is risky, to help decide where to invest in resilience upgrades. > 🚧 Work in progress. Built step by step. See [docs/plan.md](docs/plan.md). ## Docs - [Plan](docs/plan.md): architecture, tables, steps - [Decision log](docs/decisions.md): every choice and why - [Assumptions, uncertainty & scope](docs/assumptions.md) - [Design](docs/design.md) - [AI session log](docs/session/): the full conversation with the coding agent ## Run locally Requirements: Node 22+, a Supabase project. ```bash npm install cp .env.example .env.local # then fill in the values (see comments in the file) npm run db:check # verifies the database connection: lists the hubs npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 ``` ## Scripts | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `npm run dev` | Start the app locally | | `npm test` | Unit tests (Vitest) | | `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript check | | `npm run lint` | ESLint (includes the rule keeping `src/core` free of Next.js) | | `npm run db:check` | Connect to Supabase and list hubs per region | | `npm run ingest` | Fetch FEMA + Open-Meteo data for all active hubs (incremental; the first full load takes about 1 h because of Open-Meteo's rate limits) | | `npm run ingest -- --hub=dallas,denver` | Same, for selected hubs only | | `npm run ingest -- --refresh-fema` | Re-fetch FEMA records for every hub (e.g. after a new NRI release) | | `npm run score` | Re-score all hubs from stored data (no API calls). The ingest runs this automatically. | | `npm run ask -- "question"` | Ask the real agent from the terminal (add `--session=` for a follow-up, `--metric` for metric units) | | `npm run fema:anchors` | Recompute the national 95th-percentile FEMA anchors (for review before changing `scoring/config.ts`) | | `npm run session:export -- ` | Export the AI session log to `docs/session/` (scrubbed) | ## The app ![Sneakoscope: a conversation with score breakdowns, a comparison grid, seasonality strips and a premise correction](docs/screenshots/desktop-conversation.png) More screenshots: [start screen](docs/screenshots/desktop-start.png) · [phone](docs/screenshots/phone-start.png). Ask in plain language. Every number comes from deterministic, tested code, and the agent says when the data is unsure. Use the **US / Metric** switch to change units, and the side nav to reopen this browser's earlier chats. ## API Every route requires the site login (HTTP Basic Auth: `APP_USERNAME` / `APP_PASSWORD`), except the cron route. | Route | What it does | |---|---| | `POST /api/chat` | Body `{ "sessionId": null \| "", "message": "…", "units": "us" \| "metric" }`. Streams the AI SDK chat protocol: `data-session`, `data-progress`, answer text, then `data-answer` (validated) or `data-error`. | | `GET /api/widgets` | Top 5 hubs, the leading hub per hazard, data freshness. | | `GET /api/cron/ingest` | Nightly job (Vercel Cron, 06:00 UTC): fetch new weather, then re-score. Needs `Authorization: Bearer `. | Errors are always friendly JSON: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "hint", "retryable" } }`. ```bash curl -u "$APP_USERNAME:$APP_PASSWORD" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"sessionId":null,"message":"Which Midwest hubs are most exposed to winter?","units":"us"}' \ http://localhost:3000/api/chat ``` ## Evals ```bash npm run eval # 13 cases on OPENROUTER_MODEL, about 3 min, about $1 on Sonnet npm run eval -- --model=openai/gpt-6.1-terra # try another model npm run eval -- --repeat=3 # consistency check npm run eval -- --url=https://your-app.vercel.app # test a deployment npm run eval -- --no-judge # skip the independent judge ``` Prints pass/fail per case and check, plus soft metrics (tool calls, duplicates, latency, tokens, cost), and exits 1 on failure. Every answer is also graded by an **independent judge** (`JUDGE_MODEL`, a cheap model from another provider) against the actual tool results. Before each run the judge must catch 2 planted bad answers, or the report flags it as unreliable. Expected values are computed from the live data at run time. Latest results: [docs/evals.md](docs/evals.md). ## Database SQL migrations live in [supabase/migrations/](supabase/migrations/). Apply them in order to a fresh Supabase project (SQL editor or Supabase CLI). The second migration seeds the 36 hubs. ## Data attribution Weather data by [Open-Meteo.com](https://open-meteo.com/) (CC BY 4.0). Hazard data: FEMA National Risk Index.
